title: Sudden error when trying to authenticate in Vault UI via OIDC provider
body: I’m suddenly unable to complete OIDC login through the Vault UI after weeks of normal operation with Vault 1.12.2. The main window immediately says the provider window was closed before authentication completed, while the successfully authenticated pop-up ends with “Cannot read properties of null (reading 'postMessage')”. CLI OIDC authentication still works, and I can use the resulting token in the UI. The issue occurs across Brave, Chrome, Firefox, and Safari, including incognito windows and other computers. There were no Vault configuration changes or node restarts before it began. Debug logs, reverse-proxy logs, browser developer tools, and packet traces show no relevant errors or IdP traffic from the UI flow. Electing another active node, rolling-restarting all five nodes, disabling and reconfiguring OIDC, and downgrading to 1.11.4 did not change the behavior. Our test cluster is affected too.

symptoms_visible: When I click “Sign in with OIDC provider,” the main Vault window almost immediately says the provider window was closed before authentication completed.
Authentication succeeds inside the pop-up, but it then says “Cannot read properties of null (reading 'postMessage')” and the Vault UI does not complete login.
The CLI OIDC workflow completes normally, and I can use its token to log in through the UI.
I see the same UI failure in multiple browsers, incognito windows, other computers, and the test cluster; I detect no IdP traffic from the failing UI flow.
N0.label: N0 Vault UI OIDC pop-up failure reported

symptoms_visible: I can reproduce the same pop-up and postMessage errors on both macOS and Windows with Chrome, Brave, Firefox, and Safari.
N1.label: N1 platform-specific explanation ruled out

symptoms_visible: The Auth0 tutorial configuration completes login successfully from the Vault UI, but restoring a basic configuration for my own IdP brings back the same pop-up failure.
N2.label: N2 IdP-specific control test completed

symptoms_visible: In the failing pop-up, the console reports that window.opener is null when the callback calls postMessage.
The network response from my IdP contains “Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin”; using “same-origin-allow-popups” does not make the Vault login complete.
N3.label: N3 differing IdP response header isolated

symptoms_visible: When I use a Firefox extension to remove that response header temporarily, the Vault UI OIDC login completes normally.
N4.label: N4 header-removal probe succeeds

symptoms_visible: After I selectively disabled the COOP header on the IdP's OAuth-related endpoints, the Vault UI OIDC login completed normally.
N_terminal.label: terminal IdP mitigation verified

question_patterns: Which operating systems and browser versions reproduce the problem?
Can you confirm whether this is limited to one OS and browser combination?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I personally use macOS and Brave, but I have confirmed the same behavior on both Windows and macOS with Chrome, Brave, Firefox, and Safari, including other computers. It is not the macOS full-screen Firefox case someone else reported.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens in one Firefox profile on my Mac, and a clean profile works.
It reproduces on the same two operating systems, but I did not test Safari.

edges.comment: Issue comments c4-c5, describing the original reporter's systems and tests. The maintainer requested OS and browser details; the reporter confirmed that the failure crossed Windows, macOS, and multiple browser engines.

question_patterns: Can you test the Auth0 tutorial configuration as a control and report whether its UI login works?
Could you reproduce the setup with a different tutorial IdP to determine whether the failure follows your provider configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the Auth0 tutorial configuration and it worked. I then restored a basic OIDC configuration for my own IdP, and the same Vault UI problem returned.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Auth0 tutorial fails with exactly the same postMessage error.
The Auth0 tutorial works in Chrome and Firefox; my own IdP still fails in both.

edges.comment: Issue comments c6-c9, all on the original reporter's environment. The Auth0 control worked while the reporter's own IdP configuration failed, redirecting investigation from Vault cluster state toward differences in the provider flow.

question_patterns: Can you compare the response headers and pop-up console output between the working control and your failing IdP?
What does the failing pop-up's console and Network panel show when you monitor the callback?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The failing IdP response contains `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`. The pop-up console says `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'postMessage')`, and the trace reaches `window.opener.postMessage(a, window.origin)`. I also found that `same-origin-allow-popups` does not mitigate it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The working and failing IdPs return the same response headers, and window.opener is present when the callback runs.
The same header and console output appear, but I captured them in Firefox rather than Chrome.

edges.comment: Issue comment c10, from the original reporter's browser and IdP. The reporter compared the flows and supplied the raw response header, console error, and traceback. The causal interpretation that COOP severs the pop-up's opener relationship remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily neutralize the differing response header in a test browser and retry the same UI login?
Please run a controlled test without that extra provider response header and report whether the pop-up can complete.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I used a Firefox extension to remove the header from the response, and the Vault UI login completed successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Removing the header makes no difference; window.opener is still null and the login still fails.
The successful retry took a few seconds longer than the earlier attempts.

edges.comment: Issue comments c10-c11, on the original reporter's system. This is a handler-compatible configuration probe and therefore a clarification-only measurement: the reporter reports only that temporary response-header removal makes login work. The reporter additionally learned that an IdP framework update had begun injecting the header by default.

solution.intent: Correct the IdP response policy for Vault's pop-up OIDC flow by selectively omitting the restrictive Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header from OAuth-related endpoints, then verify that UI login completes.
solution.concrete_example: Configure the IdP or its reverse proxy not to emit `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` on the OAuth/OIDC endpoints used by Vault. Retest “Sign in with OIDC provider” and confirm that the callback can message the main Vault window and finish login.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw header, null-window.opener traceback, working Auth0 control, and successful header-removal probe. Inferring that `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` isolates the IdP pop-up so Vault's callback cannot call `window.opener.postMessage` is the diagnostic conclusion.

edges.comment: Issue comments c10-c13 resolve the original reporter's chain: an IdP framework update started injecting COOP by default, and the reporter restored normal operation by selectively disabling it for OAuth-related endpoints. Later comments describe other providers, extensions, browser containers, and deployments; they are independent reports and are not spliced into this reporter's resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the reporter's IdP began returning `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`, which isolated Vault's OIDC pop-up and left `window.opener` null when the callback attempted `postMessage`.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the working Auth0 control, the failing IdP's response header and callback trace, and the successful temporary header-removal test.

Must recommend selectively removing or disabling the restrictive COOP header on the IdP's OAuth/OIDC endpoints; `same-origin-allow-popups` must not be presented as a verified fix because it did not mitigate this case.

Must not recommend Vault failover, cluster restart, OIDC reconfiguration, version downgrade, browser switching, incognito mode, or pop-up-blocker changes as the resolution; those directions were already falsified by the reporter's evidence.
Must have the reporter verify that the Vault UI OIDC flow completes after the IdP-side change before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical Vault operator comfortable administering a five-node cluster, reconfiguring auth methods, tracing network traffic, inspecting browser developer tools, comparing HTTP headers, and changing IdP endpoint behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical, and persistent; reports negative results explicitly, follows requested control tests, and supplies reproducible technical evidence before proposing a cause.
